⟪1.⟫ as conjc., continuing a negation or prohibition, ⟪but not⟫, ⟪and not⟫, ⟪nor⟫: preceded by μή, ⟦Matthew 6:25|Mt 6:25⟧ ⟦Matthew 22:29|22:29⟧, ⟦Mark 12:24|Mk 12:24⟧, ⟦Luke 14:12|Lk 14:12⟧, al.; ἵνα μή, ⟦John 4:15|Jo 4:15⟧; ὅπως μή, ⟦Luke 16:26|Lk 16:26⟧; μηδέ . . . μηδέ, ⟪neither . . . nor⟫, ⟦Matthew 10:10|Mt 10:10⟧, ⟦1 Corinthians 10:8|I Co 10:8⟧, ⟦1 Corinthians 10:9|9⟧.
⟪2.⟫ As adv., strengthening a negation, ⟪not even⟫: ⟦Mark 2:2|Mk 2:2⟧, ⟦1 Corinthians 5:11|I Co 5:11⟧, al.

G3367.b:

G3379.b:
⟪μήποτε⟫
(= μή ποτε, and so written in WH, exc. ⟦Matthew 25:9|Mt 25:9⟧), negative particle,
related to οὔποτε as μή to οὐ.
⟪1.⟫ As neg. particle, ⟪never⟫: ⟦Hebrews 9:17|He 9:17⟧ (R, mg., but v. infr.; WH, txt., μή τότε).
⟪2.⟫ As conjc., ⟪lest ever⟫, ⟪lest haply⟫ (the idea of chance rather than of time seems to prevail in NT): ⟦Matthew 4:6|Mt 4:6⟧(LXX) ⟦Matthew 5:25|5:25⟧ ⟦Matthew 7:6|7:6⟧ ⟦Matthew 13:15|13:15⟧(LXX), ⟦Matthew 13:29|29⟧ ⟦Matthew 15:32|15:32⟧ ⟦Matthew 27:64|27:64⟧, ⟦Mark 4:12|Mk 4:12⟧(LXX) ⟦Mark 14:2|14:2⟧, ⟦Luke 4:11|Lk 4:11⟧ ⟦Luke 12:58|12:58⟧ ⟦Luke 14:12|14:12⟧, ⟦Luke 14:29|29⟧, ⟦Acts 28:27|Ac 28:27⟧; after verbs of fearing or taking heed, ⟦Luke 21:34|Lk 21:34⟧, ⟦Hebrews 2:1|He 2:1⟧ ⟦Hebrews 3:12|3:12⟧ ⟦Hebrews 4:1|4:1⟧; with ellipse of the verb or ptcp., ⟦Luke 14:8|Lk 14:8⟧, ⟦Acts 5:39|Ac 5:39⟧; in later writers (v. M, Pr., 192 f.), ⟪perhaps⟫, ⟦Matthew 25:9|Mt 25:9⟧.
⟪3.⟫ As interrogative;
	⟪(a)⟫ in direct questions, like μή, expecting a negative answer: ⟦John 7:26|Jo 7:26⟧, ⟦Hebrews 9:17|He 9:17⟧, (R, txt., cf. Westc., in l.; but v. supr.);
	⟪(b)⟫ in indirect questions, ⟪whether haply⟫, ⟪if haply⟫: ⟦Luke 3:15|Lk 3:15⟧, ⟦2 Timothy 2:25|II Ti 2:25⟧.†
